text: . The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

. The External Affairs Ministry has said, three more Indian nationals, including a five-year-old child, have been rescued from the flood-hit Trishuli Bazaar area of Nepal, bringing the total count of Indian evacuees to 169.Sharing broader updates on the safety of Indian nationals while briefing media in New Delhi yesterday, MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, 275 Indian nationals remain missing.He noted that 1,907 Indians have safely crossed over to Nepal from China. Mr Jaiswal said that the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu is facilitating the return of Indian evacuees on flights back home. He said, there are no Indian travelers who are stranded in the Tibetan Autonomous Region.The spokesperson said India has supplied around 95 tonnes of relief material to Nepal since the devastating flash floods hit the country on 26th of last month.The MEA spokesperson said India will continue to provide assistance to Nepal as per the requirements of the government in that country. He said, in the coming days, India is planning to send more forensic kits, Bailey bridges, and other materials that are requested by the government of Nepal.Meanwhile, the death toll from the floods in the Himalayan nation has crossed 1340 after rescue workers recovered more bodies from affected areas.While emergency teams have rescued more than 12,000 people, roughly 5,000 remain missing as search and rescue operations continue.

. The US trade deficit in goods and services surged 24.4 per cent in July, to 88.6 billion US dollars. That is higher than the upwardly revised figure of 71.2 billion US dollars recorded in June, according to data from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) and the US Census Bureau. The increase came as US imports rose, while exports declined. Exports fell 2.1 per cent to 310.7 billion US dollars, while imports climbed 2.8 per cent to 399.3 billion US dollars.The US also recorded a five-billion-dollar goods trade deficit with India in July. The largest US goods trade deficit was with Mexico, at 27.5 billion US dollars, followed by Vietnam, Taiwan, China, South Korea and the European Union. The services sector provided a relatively small offset to the widening goods deficit. Services exports declined by 0.4 billion billion US dollars to 109.7 billion, while services imports fell by 0.6 billion US dollars to 78.7 billion.

. In Shooting, the Indian team will be attending its final training camp ahead of the Asian Games 2026 starting later this month in Japan. The camp begins at the Madhya Pradesh State Shooting Academy in Bhopal today.A total of 18 shooters, including nine men and nine women, will be taking part in the camp. The squad includes top shooters such as Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh, and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar.Expert coaches will be training the shooters in rifle and pistol events. The camp will be focusing on shooting skills, fitness, recovery, and mental strength. The shooters will also be training at modern 10, 25, and 50-metre ranges.A special training camp was held in Bhopal last month as well. The Indian shooting team will leave for the Asian Games after the camp concludes on 14th September.

. The Goa Government will launch the ‘Goa Ujjwala Scheme’ on September 5, providing financial assistance equivalent to the cost of three domestic LPG cylinders every year to eligible household LPG and PNG consumers. Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said ₹3,000 will be directly transferred into beneficiaries’ bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).The Civil Supplies Department has made a provision of ₹100 crore for the scheme. There is no income criterion for availing the benefit. However, only one domestic gas connection per family will be eligible. Existing Griha Aadhar and Deen Dayal Social Security Scheme beneficiaries can apply by submitting the scheme application and bank passbook. A separate application will be available for open-category beneficiaries. Applications will be available at panchayat and municipal offices. The first instalment is expected to be credited to beneficiaries’ bank accounts on September 9 or 10.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said India is in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia. He said New Delhi is exploring ideas and suggestions that could help mitigate or end the conflict.Dr Jaishankar made the remarks while addressing a joint press conference with Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski following their talks in Warsaw yesterday.The External Affairs Minister reiterated that India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war. He said wars have no winners and only lead to more deaths, destruction and global costs.He added that efforts should focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. He said India is committed to doing whatever it can to help bring the conflict to an end.Dr Jaishankar reached Poland after visiting Ukraine, where he held talks with top Ukrainian leadership on Thursday.During the media briefing, the External Affairs Minister said he discussed with his Polish counterpart the complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security.Both sides also reviewed the progress of the Joint Action Plan 2024-28, which focuses on trade and investment, defence, culture and multilateral cooperation.Later, Dr Jaishankar also called on Polish President Karol Nawrocki and discussed the bilateral Strategic Partnership and exchanged views on the Ukraine conflict and the West Asia situation.In Kyiv, Dr Jaishankar said that India is ready to extend any help in any manner to end the Ukraine-Russia war. He had also met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv on Thursday.After talks with the External Affairs Minister, President Zelenskyy said that he was grateful to India for its commitment to ending the war.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that India is moving forward towards making India the world’s largest sporting hub. The Minister said this during the inauguration of World Archery Para Series in Ahmedabad, Gujarat through video conferencing from New Delhi. Mr Shah said that India will emerge as major hubs of the sporting world in the coming days. He added, India will also become a hub for training in all kinds of sports, as well as for the production of sports facilities and equipment.The Minister said that the government aims not merely to win the maximum number of medals, but to strengthen all the sports included in the Olympics, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, Police Games, and other such competitions. Mr Shah said that athletes from 19 countries, including Bhutan, the United Kingdom, China, Bangladesh, France, Germany, Indonesia and the United States, are participating in these games. He further said that the 2030 Commonwealth Games will mark the centenary edition of the Games, and expressed pride that Ahmedabad will host the event.

. The three-day BRICS Chief Justices’ Forum has begun in New Delhi. The three day forum serves as a platform for participating judiciaries to discuss contemporary issues concerning justice delivery, international dispute resolution, technology and sustainable development, while facilitating an exchange of views among judicial leaders.The forum has brought together Chief Justices, Presidents of Supreme Courts and senior judicial leaders from BRICS Member States and Partner Countries. As part of the Forum, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant today held a series of bilateral meetings with heads of judicial delegations from various countries including, Russia, China, the UAE, South Africa, Iran and Uzbekistan. Discussions were held for strengthening of judicial cooperation among countries, technology advancement integration for increasing efficiency of judiciary, enhancing people-to-people ties through expeditious judicial processes and best legal practices of different countries.

. At the China Masters badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty entered their fourth-straight China Masters semifinal after beating Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen 21-13, 16-21, 21-18 in Shenzhen this evening.The Indian pair defeated France’s Toma Junior Popov and Christo Popov 21-17, 22-24, 21-9, last night, to make it to the quarterfinal.In men’s singles Kidambi Srikanth’s campaign at the China Masters, ended after losing 16-21, 16-21 to Lee Cheuk Yiu of Hong Kong in the quarterfinals in Shenzhen today.Earlier, India’s women’s singles campaign came to an end yesterday after Tanvi Sharma lost 21-17, 18-21, 21-16 against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki.

. India’s services sector strengthened in August, supported by resilient export demand, while employment reached a 15-month high. The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) Business Activity Index rose to 54.1 in August, up from 53.3 in July. Despite the acceleration, the overall pace of expansion remained the second-weakest since March 2022, and stayed marginally below the long-run average of 54.5.The report noted that new business gained momentum in August due to stronger customer demand and marketing initiatives. However, the growth rate in sales was the second-slowest in nearly four-and-a-half-years, impacted by challenging market conditions and softer client appetite in selected services.According to the latest data compiled by S&P Global, input cost inflation edged up slightly last month due to higher spending on digital platforms, electricity, inputs, labour, marketing and regulatory requirements.Meanwhile, the HSBC India Composite PMI Output Index stood at 54.3 in August, unchanged from July, as faster growth in services offset a slowdown in manufacturing.

. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called upon the automotive industry to deepen localisation, expand exports and prepare to serve global markets. The Minister was addressing the 66th Society of Indian Automobile Manufactures-SIAM Annual Convention in New Delhi yesterday. He urged the industry to seize the opportunities emerging from India’s expanding trade partnerships, growing domestic market and global shifts in manufacturing.Mr Goyal said the automotive sector would be one of the most important drivers of India’s growth story in the years to come. He said the industry had demonstrated strong growth and that rising incomes and aspirations offered considerable scope for this growth to continue. The Commerce and Industry Minister said the AI will help the automotive industry become more efficient, competitive and customer-friendly. He added that the government is ready to support industry with critical minerals, technology, plug-and-play infrastructure and industrial parks.

. Authorities in Australia have confirmed Sydney’s first case of the highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu strain. It is the first confirmed case in Sydney since H5N1 reached mainland Australia in June. Authorities have advised residents with pet birds or backyard chickens to avoid contact with wild birds. Dog owners have also been urged to prevent their pets from chasing or eating wild bird carcasses.Northern Beaches Mayor Sue Heins warned that more cases could follow and said the region should prepare for potentially serious impacts on wildlife. Federal data shows 468 confirmed H5N1 events across Australia as of Wednesday, including 20 in New South Wales. No cases have been detected so far in commercial poultry, captive birds or livestock in the state. The World Health Organisation says H5N1 primarily affects birds but can also infect mammals, including humans. Human infections can range from mild illnesses to severe and, in some cases, fatal diseases.

. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi interacted with the recipients of the National Teachers Awards 2026 last evening. Mr Joshi said teachers must prepare children to help build a Viksit Bharat by 2047.He said students are the nation’s greatest wealth and should be groomed to become well-rounded individuals.On the occasion, Mr Joshi hosted a dinner in honour of the awardees. Ministers of State for Education Jayant Singh and Dr Sukanta Majumdar also attended the event.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today, snapping a four-session losing streak. The Sensex climbed 363 points or half a per cent to close at 76,515, while the Nifty added 24 points or 0.1 per cent to settle at 23,898. However, in the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 0.2 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index gained 0.2 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened with a gap-up amid positive global cues. Both benchmark indices remained in the green throughout the session, trading within a narrow range. However, following the closing auction session, the indices pared some of their gains.In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 companies logged gains. Among the top movers, Tata Steel jumped 2.9 per cent, Reliance gained 1.6 per cent and Bajaj Finance advanced one and a half per cent. In contrast, Bharti Airtel as well as HCL Tech declined 1.2 per cent, Eternal dropped 1.1 per cent and Asian Paints lost half a per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 16 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top performers, Housing Finance, Metal, Telecommunication and Insurance rose 1.4 per cent, Commodities and Financial Services gained 0.6 per cent and Private Banks Index added half a per cent. In contrast, Realty and Capital Goods declined 0.7 per cent, Healthcare fell half a per cent and Hospitals lost 0.4 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2388 companies advanced, 1991 declined and 239 remained unchanged.

. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni today thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his wishes on her government becoming the longest-serving in the history of the Italian Republic.In a social media post on X, Meloni expressed confidence that India and Italy will continue to strengthen the bond between the two continents and work together to develop the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.Meloni’s response came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated his Italian counterpart on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy’s postwar history.  In a social media post, Mr Modi said that this milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership.The Prime Minister emphasized that her friendship has also been instrumental in strengthening the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership. Mr Modi further said that he looks forward to continuing close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of both the countries. He extended his wishes for the continued success of Giorgia Meloni in the years ahead.

. President Droupadi Murmu has called upon teachers and educators to continually update their knowledge, embrace technology, and adopt innovative teaching methods.In her message on the occasion of Teachers’ Day today, the President said teachers and educators play a vital role in nurturing talent and strengthening character through their guidance and mentorship.She said, dedicated and caring teachers can recognise the unique potential of students, inspire them, and encourage them to strive for excellence. President Murmu also urged teachers to promote independent thinking and cultivate a spirit of enquiry among students.Expressing gratitude to all dedicated teachers for their contributions, the President wished them continued success in nurturing enlightened generations who will take the nation to greater heights.President Murmu also paid tribute to former President Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. She described him as an extraordinary teacher.Teachers’ Day is observed every year on 5th of September to mark the birth anniversary of former President Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who was a renowned educationist, author, and philosopher. The day honours the vital role of teachers and educators in nation-building.Teachers transform the lives of students, shape generations, and strengthen the foundations of society.On the occasion, President Droupadi Murmu will confer the National Teachers’ Awards on 48 school teachers in New Delhi this morning. The 48 selected teachers are from 27 States, seven Union Territories, and six Central Government organisations.The President will also present National Awards to 21 teachers and faculty members from higher education institutions and polytechnics.Twelve teachers and faculty members are from Central Higher Education Institutions, five from state universities, including three government and two private colleges, and four from polytechnics, including two government and two private polytechnics. Short documentaries showcasing the exemplary work of each awardee will also be screened at the event.

. The 5th Sohra International Half Marathon 2026 was successfully held today, bringing together regional, national, and international athletes to Meghalaya.The event was organised by the Meghalaya State Olympics Association (MSOA) in collaboration with the Directorate of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya, Meghalaya Athletics Association and an official recognised by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).The 2026 edition saw the registration of 11,672 runners across all categories. Participation included international athletes and runners from other states as well.In his keynote address,Wailadmiki Shylla, Minister, Department of Sports and YouthAffairs, Government of Meghalaya highlighted the event’s remarkable evolution from a modest starting field of 750 runners to nearly 12,000 participants.Welcoming athletes representing almost 24 states across the country, Shylla emphasized the marathon’s  widespread socio-economic impact, which directly benefits local homestay operators, transport providers, and farmers, while establishing Sohra as a top-tier sporting destination beyond its traditional fame for rainand waterfalls.Sukant Suki Singh, the first Indian to Complete three 200-Mile Ultramarathons, praisedMeghalaya’s exceptional sports infrastructure and natural beauty, identifying the state as the future sporting capital of India.He specifically commended Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangmafor completely transforming the region’s sports landscape and actively nurturing athletic talent from a young age.The Sohra Half Marathon witnessed strong performances across all its competitive categories, with Satish Kumar Verma emerging winner in the Elite Men’s 21 km category with a timing of 1:03:04, and Tejaswini Narendra Lambkane claiming the Elite Women’s title in 1:15:20.

. The death toll from the devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods has surged to 1,287.  According to Nepal Police, the highest number of fatalities have been reported in Chitwan at 359, followed by Nawalparasi East with 219, Nawalparasi West with 212, Nuwakot with 184, Rasuwa with 140, Gorkha with 72, Dhading with 63 and Tanahu with 38. Two additional deaths occurred while victims were undergoing treatment at hospitals in Kathmandu.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) reported that as of last evening, 5,083 people were reported missing. Meanwhile, Nepal has also begun using DNA tests to identify victims.In a remarkable rescue effort, two men were rescued alive from a tunnel at Nepal’s Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project, 10 days after being trapped there in the wake of the Bhotekoshi flash floods. According to the Nepal Army’s Public Relations Directorate, the operation was intensified after rescuers heard voices from inside the tunnel and established communication with those believed to be trapped. Emergency teams have rescued more than 12,000 people so far.The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on 26th of last month, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal, leaving a trail of destruction.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi rose nearly 0.3 per cent while Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 0.2 per cent. In European markets, Germany’s DAX was trading almost flat, and London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.4 per cent, when reports last came in.

. In badminton, India’s ace shuttler Kidambi Srikanth will face Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu tomorrow in the men’s singles quarterfinals at the China Masters Super 750 in Shenzhen. Srikanth beat Canada’s world No. 9 Victor Lai 21-18, 21-19 today.Earlier, India’s top men’s doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty overcame a mid-match wobble to beat French brothers Christo and Toma Junior Popov 21-15 22-24 21-9 and progress to the quarterfinals. Teenager Tanvi Sharma bowed out in the Round of 16 after a three-game loss to Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki in women’s singles, while Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were eliminated in mixed doubles.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi today. Mr Modi will also address the gathering on the occasion.Shri Ram College of Commerce, part of the University of Delhi, is one of India’s premier institutions of higher education. It is a distinguished centre of learning in Commerce, Economics, and Management.Established in 1926 by eminent industrialist and philanthropist Sir Shri Ram, the college has nurtured generations of scholars, professionals, administrators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, and nation-builders over the past century.The centenary celebrations coincide with Teachers’ Day. This makes the occasion particularly significant as the nation honours the contribution of teachers and educators in shaping generations and strengthening the foundations of society.

. In Women’s Cricket, the Indian team has entered the semifinals of the T-20 Asia Cup after a massive 137-run victory over Hong Kong in Dubai last night. Batting first, India scored 193 for 5 in 20 overs, powered by Smriti Mandhana’s historic 124 runs off just 64 balls. She was named the Player of the Match.With this spectacular performance, Mandhana broke multiple world records, overtaking Mithali Raj to become the highest run-scorer in women’s international cricket and securing the record for the most international centuries by a female batter. In response, Hong Kong was bowled out for a mere 56 runs in 16.2 overs, with India’s Deepti Sharma taking 3 wickets, while Prema Rawat, Shree Charani, and Nandini Sharma took 2 wickets each. Following this dominant win, the Indian team will now shift their focus to their next exciting group match against Afghanistan on September 13.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 0.4 per cent down at 95 US dollars and 10 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.6 per cent lower at 90 US dollars and 76 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The International Cricket Council today moved the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 to India from Sri Lanka. The six-team event will be played in Mumbai and Vadodara from 14th to 28th of February.Sri Lanka was dropped as host as the sport is grappling with governance issues in the island nation, with the ICC Board approving India as the new host.The tournament will bring together six of the world’s leading women’s cricket teams, Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka. These six teams have qualified for the tournament as per their positions in the ICC Women’s T20 International Team Rankings on the 6th of July qualification cut-off date. They will compete in a round-robin league, with the top two sides advancing to the final on 28th February.ICC Chairman,Jay Shah, said, the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket. He said, as the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage.India hosted the Women’s ODI World Cup last year when the home team won a pathbreaking title.

. At least 40 Yemeni government soldiers and 50 Houthi fighters have been killed in fierce fighting across the country’s western frontlines since Thursday, reports said today. A medical official on the Red Sea coastal front in Hodeidah province said 14 government soldiers have been killed since the Houthis launched a large-scale offensive early today. Separately, another medical official on the front in the neighbouring Taiz province said 26 government soldiers have been killed in clashes that began Thursday and continued into today.Meanwhile, medical sources in Houthi-controlled areas said hospitals in Hodeidah have received the bodies of at least 50 Houthi fighters killed on the Hodeidah and Taiz fronts, report said. The escalation intensified today as both sides sent more troops, armoured vehicles and equipment to the two fronts, according to military sources. The latest escalation marks some of the heaviest ground fighting in western Yemen in recent years, raising concerns of a broader return to large-scale hostilities after years of relative calm across many of the country’s frontlines.Fighting between government forces and the Houthis has intensified across several fronts in recent weeks. The government forces stepped up drone and artillery strikes on Houthi positions, while the group launched missile and drone attacks on government-held areas in Marib and along the western Red Sea coast.

. In the United States, a federal judge has extended a ban stopping President Donald Trump’s administration from implementing a new US Postal Service rule to restrict mail voting ahead of the midterm elections in November.Judge Indira Talwani issued the order yesterday. The Trump administration has said it will appeal the decision and has asked the US Supreme Court to intervene.The ruling comes as states begin sending mail-in ballots. North Carolina started mailing ballots yesterday. Other states are expected to follow soon.Election officials have warned that changing voting rules at this stage could confuse. They said it could also prevent some voters from receiving or returning their ballots on time.Judge Talwani said the changes could affect millions of voters. She noted that states must send out ballots within fixed deadlines.The order allows states to voluntarily adopt the Postal Service’s new system. However, no state has announced plans to do so. President Trump has repeatedly criticised mail-in voting and sought to limit its use.The issue has led to several legal challenges and could affect the upcoming midterm elections, where control of Congress is at stake.

. President Droupadi Murmu has greeted teachers across the country on the eve of Teachers’ Day. In her message, the President said that Teachers’ Day is observed to mark the birth anniversary of former President Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who was a great author and philosopher. President Murmu paid her tributes to Dr Radhakrishnan and described him as an extraordinary teacher. The President said teachers play a vital role in nurturing talent and strengthening character through their guidance and mentorship.Expressing her gratitude to all the dedicated teachers for their contribution, she wished that all teachers would nurture enlightened generations who will take the nation to greater heights.The President will confer National Teachers Awards on 48 school teachers in New Delhi tomorrow on the occasion of Teachers’ Day. The 48 selected school teachers are from 27 States, seven Union Territories and six Organizations of the Central Government.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. US defence giant GE Aerospace has delivered a fresh batch of three F404-IN20 engines to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), providing a crucial boost to the country’s domestic Tejas Mk1A fighter jet programme. The F404 engines are being supplied under a 2021 contract between HAL and GE Aerospace for 99 power plants intended to equip the initial fleet of Tejas Mk1A jets. The programme has grappled with years of delivery bottlenecks stemming from international supply chain constraints, which previously left completed airframes waiting on engine integration.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. In Badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will take on the Malaysian duo of Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong in the semi-final of the China Masters in Shenzhen today.The Indian pair defeated Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen 21-13, 16-21, 21-18 in the quarter-final yesterday. With the victory, Satwik and Chirag reached the semi-finals of the China Masters for the fourth consecutive time.On the other hand their Malaysian opponents, Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong, pulled off a major upset by defeating Indonesia’s world No. 7 pair, Sabar Karyaman Gutama and Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani, 21-17, 16-21, 21-19.The victory earned them their first-ever Super 750 semi-final appearance.Meanwhile, India’s campaign in the singles events came to an end as Kidambi Srikanth lost to Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu in the Men’s Singles quarter-final. In Women’s Singles, Tanvi Sharma went down against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves surged by 11.4 billion US dollars to a record high of 740.8 billion dollars during the week ended 28th of last month.According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 9.3 billion US dollars to 600.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves added 2.1 billion dollars to 116.4 billion dollars.However, Special Drawing Rights declined by 43 million dollars to 18.8 billion dollars. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 11 million dollars to 4.9 billion dollars.

. India has announced the decision to appoint a Defence Attache to Brussels complementing Belgium placing a Defence Attache in New Delhi earlier this year. Briefing media on Belgian Prime Minister, Bart De Wever’s India visit, Secretary (West) in External Affairs Ministry, Sibi George yesterday affirmed that significant progress will be seen in defence engagement between the two nations, including in defence production.He said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Belgian Prime Minister have set a target to double bilateral trade in the next five years in the backdrop of successful conclusion of India-EU FTA. Currently the trade is about 13 billion US dollars. Secretary (West) emphasised that there is a clear focus on three Ts – Trade, Technology and Talent. Mr George informed that Prime Minister Modi has invited the Belgian universities and premier academic institutions to open campuses in India. Mr George said that Prime Minister Modi also invited Belgium to participate in the WAVES 2.0. Replying to a query, Secretary (West) informed that both sides exchanged views on major international developments, including the recent developments in Ukraine and West Asia.He said, regarding Ukraine, both sides reaffirmed support for efforts towards the achievement of a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace through dialogue and diplomacy. On West Asia, they discussed the recent developments in the region and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomatic engagement to address challenges in a peaceful manner.

. The government has proposed allowing up to three-year permissions for importing and transporting petroleum in ISO tank containers and introducing a seven-working-day deemed approval mechanism for complete applications as part of proposed amendments to the Petroleum Rules, 2002.The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas issued a draft notification on Thursday, proposing the Petroleum (Amendment) Rules, 2026.The ministry has invited objections and suggestions on the draft, which will be considered after the expiry of 30 days from the date the Gazette copies are made available to the public.Under the proposed changes, no person would be allowed to import an ISO tank container filled or intended to be filled with petroleum without obtaining permission from the Chief Controller or Controller.Applications would have to be submitted through the online licensing portal of the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), along with specified technical and safety documents.The objections and suggestions, if any, may be addressed to the Joint Secretary (M&OR), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, New Delhi-110001 or sent by email at: js.mkt-png@gov.in.

. US President Donald Trump said his special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine to push for a peace deal aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war.Speaking to reporters at the Oval Office, President Trump said the two negotiators will assess whether progress can be made between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.President Trump said his administration would present an idea for peace and stressed that the heavy military losses make a settlement urgent. The visits are part of Washington’s wider efforts to bring Russia and Ukraine to the negotiating table and end the conflict.In a social media post, the Ukrainian President said the US delegation is expected to visit Moscow first and Kyiv next. He said Ukraine will ensure their safe travel and has called on Russia to avoid air strikes during the talks.

. In Women’s Cricket, India will take on arch-rivals Pakistan in the final Group A clash of the T20 Asia Cup at the Dubai International Stadium tonight. The match will begin at 8 PM Indian Standard Time.India have already secured a place in the semi-finals after recording convincing victories over Thailand and Hong Kong in their previous two matches.The Indian team will now look to maintain its winning run and finish the group stage with a perfect record.Pakistan, meanwhile, have played just one match. They began their campaign with a win over Thailand.The team currently has two points in Group A and needs just one more point from its remaining two matches to qualify for the semi-finals. Their last league game is against Hong Kong.Last night, Hosts United Arab Emirates (UAE) defeated Indonesia by six wickets at the Dubai International Stadium. Chasing a target of 72 runs, the UAE overhauled the score, posting 75 for the loss of four wickets in 13.1 overs.Earlier, put in to bat, Indonesia were bowled out for 71 in 19.4 overs.

. In badminton, India’s ace shuttler Kidambi Srikanth will take on Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu in the Men’s Singles Quarterfinals at the China Masters Super 750 in Shenzhen today. Srikanth defeated world No. 9 Victor Lai of Canada, 21-18, 21-19, yesterday.India’s top Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty progressed to the quarterfinals. They overcame a mid-match wobble to beat French brothers Christo and Toma Junior Popov 21-15, 22-24, and 21-9. However, in Women’s Singles, teenager Tanvi Sharma bowed out in the Round of 16 after a three-game loss to Japan’s Tomoka Miyazak. Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were also eliminated from Mixed Doubles.

. Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has stated that Belgium will work towards strengthening maritime cooperation with India and announced that a full Belgian delegation from the maritime and port sector would visit India in February next year, with steps to be taken towards undertaking concrete work in this area. He was addressing the India-Belgium high-level discussions on the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement held in Mumbai today. He said the Free Trade Agreement is a symbol of strategic openness, trust and mutual respect and expressed confidence that it would further strengthen the economies of both India and the European Union and help them remain resilient amid global uncertainty.Prime Minister Bart De Wever asserted that at a time when the world is witnessing increasingly violent conflicts, strengthening trade relations between strong partner countries is the only answer. He stressed that safe and reliable maritime supply chains have become twice as important in such circumstances, and that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement comes at a particularly crucial time. He expressed confidence that the agreement would provide a foundation on which many major initiatives could be built in the future. He also criticised countries that impose unilateral and unfair tariffs on others.Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said Maharashtra would play a very important role in the journey towards doubling bilateral trade between India and Belgium. He called upon Belgian companies looking towards India following the India-EU Free Trade Agreement to consider Maharashtra as their preferred base for entering the Indian market. He proposed setting up a team to identify a select number of projects between Belgium and Maharashtra and fast-track their implementation. He also invited Belgium to be part of Maharashtra’s journey towards becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2030.Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said that the economies of Belgium and India are complementary in five key areas – diamonds and jewellery, semiconductors, green hydrogen and ports, defence and advanced manufacturing, and agriculture and food processing. He said that in the face of global uncertainty, there are only two choices – to be swept away by the prevailing instability or to build bridges of trust. He affirmed that India and Belgium have chosen to come together and work towards the latter.Representatives of various companies, diplomatic officials and others were present on the occasion.

. The National Testing Agency (NTA) has released admit cards for candidates appearing for UGC-NET June 2026 in English, Commerce and Sociology on the 9th and 10th of this month. Candidates can download their admit cards from ugcnet.ta.nic.in using their login credentials.The NTA announced re-test for three papers of the UGC-NET examination, English, Commerce and Sociology following complaints about several errors in these papers.The English paper will be held on 9th September from 9 AM to 12 noon in Shift 1, while the Commerce paper will be conducted the same day from 3 PM to 6 PM in Shift 2. The Sociology paper will be held on 10th September from 9 AM to 12 noon in Shift 1.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. At the Pickleball World Cup 2026, India remained unbeaten on the opening day of the Team Event in Da Nang, Vietnam. The tournament is being held till the 6th of this month. This marks the end of the league stage, where a dominant India defeated Antigua and Barbuda, Israel and the Czech Republic. The Indian Pro squad recorded dominant victories over Antigua and Barbuda and Israel, winning both ties 6-0. India then defeated the Czech Republic 5-1 to top the league stage.The team will now face Portugal in the Round of 32. India’s Senior squad also had a strong start, defeating Germany and Nepal 4-0 each to advance to the Round of 32. India has bagged a total of 37 medals so far in the tournament, including six gold, 16 silver and 15 bronze. Unbeaten through the team league stage, India is currently at the 4th spot in the medal tally.

. Wall Street ended higher yesterday, after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to support holding rates steady barring any surprises in upcoming inflation data. Among the major indices, the Nasdaq Composite surged 1.4 per cent the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2 per cent, and the S&P 500 gained 1.1 per cent.On the economic front, the unemployment insurance weekly claims increased by 2,000 to 2 lakh six thousand in the week ending August 29, according to the data released by US Department of Labour.Market participants closely watch the upcoming nonfarm payrolls data to gauge the Federal Reserve’s next policy stance.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

The UN General Assembly has voted to replace the traditional world map with one that more accurately reflects the size of Africa.The “Correct the Map” resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by African Union (AU) members, passed with the support of 164 nations, including France and the UK. The United States was the only nation to vote against it while six countries abstained.The UN vote is non-binding, but it will encourage governments and institutions to stop using the traditional Mercator map.The Mercator map, which has been in common use since the 16th Century, has come in for criticism as it shows Africa as similar in size to Greenland, even though it is 14 times larger. Critics say this leads to the development needs and potential for countries near the equator to be minimised.The Mercator map was designed in 1569 by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European explorers navigate across the world.The map makes countries near the poles appear much larger than they really are. The distortion of his map is a result of the fact that it is impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.In an effort to correct this, a team of cartographers in 2018 created an equal area map they called the Equal Earth projection which shows the relative sizes of continents more accurately. In February, the African Union’s 54 member states adopted it, and said it more accurately represents the sizes of all continents, particularly Africa.Ahead of the voting, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey talking to the media, said a fair world begins with a fair map. At a UN briefing, Mr Dussey said, a map is never neutral. It shapes perceptions and influences how the place of peoples and continents in the world is understood.France has also backed the change and said it plans to stop using the Mercator map. However, the United States criticised the UN vote, arguing that the General Assembly should focus on more serious global issues.Campaigners say maps are more than just guides for travellers, they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically.

. The Miss World 2026 finale will be held in the coastal city of Nha Trang in Vietnam today. A total of 111 contestants are competing for the coveted crown. Miss World 2025 winner Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand will crown her successor.India is being represented by Nikita Porwal, the 2024 Femina Miss India World winner. Nikita, who hails from Madhya Pradesh, started her career as a television anchor.She later moved into theatre and pageantry. India last won the Miss World title in 2017, when Manushi Chhillar was crowned the winner. Nikita will now aim to bring the prestigious crown back to India.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.
